title: Pinrail plugin manifest
description: The manifest.json at the root of a plugin's folder. Paths in it are relative to that folder and cannot leave it.

$schema.description: This schema's URL, for an editor to check the manifest as you write it.

name.description: The plugin's identifier: agents submit to it, and it is unique among installed plugins. Lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter.

version.description: A semantic version such as `"1.2.0"`. The major version is a promise to every review created under it.

pinrail.description: The oldest Pinrail the plugin works with, such as `">=0.1"`. An older app refuses the plugin and names the version it needs.

title.description: What the app calls the plugin in its lists and settings. Defaults to `name`.

description.description: A sentence on what the plugin is for.

use_when.description: When an agent should ask with this plugin, in one line: what situation it is for. `pinrail plugins` shows it to an agent choosing a plugin.

example.description: A JSON file beside the manifest holding a payload that passes payload_schema, shown to an agent as a starting point. Keep it to the fewest items that show the shape: agents read it whole. One that does not pass costs the plugin the example, not its place.

sample.description: A request file beside the manifest, in the shape `pinrail submit --request` reads: a `title`, a `payload` that passes payload_schema, and the `attachments` it names, relative to the file. `pinrail submit <plugin> --sample` and Settings send it, so anyone can see the plugin without writing a payload. Keep it out of `fixtures/`, which installs leave behind. One that does not load costs the plugin the sample, not its place.

icon.description: An SVG file beside the manifest, shown beside the plugin's reviews, such as `icon.svg`. The app draws it in the text's colour at 13 to 16 px, as it draws its own Lucide icons: a 24 × 24 outline in `currentColor` fits best. At most 32 KB. One that does not load costs the plugin its icon, not its place.

payload_schema.description: What an agent must send: a JSON Schema 2020-12, inline or `{"$ref": "schemas/payload.schema.json"}`. A payload that fails it never reaches the inbox.

decision_schema.description: What the view hands back: a JSON Schema 2020-12, inline or by `$ref`. A decision that fails it goes back to the view as violations.

min_height.description: The smallest height, in pixels, the app gives the view.

settings_schema.description: The plugin's own settings, each a row in Settings › Plugins: an object schema of booleans, strings and numbers, each with a default, inline or by `$ref`. A schema that breaks these rules costs the plugin its settings, not its place.

shortcuts.description: The keys the view answers: listed in the app's keyboard help and forwarded when the view's frame has no focus. A list that breaks these rules costs the plugin its shortcuts.

keys.description: Modifiers (`cmd`, `ctrl`, `alt`, `shift`, or `cmdorctrl` for cmd on macOS and ctrl on Linux) joined by `+` in any order, then one key: `j`, `cmd+shift+f`, `escape`.

does.description: The one-line label the keyboard help shows.

group.description: Lists the entry under this caption.

decision_template.description: A MiniJinja file that renders a decision as markdown, for the command's markdown output and Copy as markdown. A template that does not compile costs the plugin the template.

request.description: What a review asks, counted from its payload when it is submitted.

outcome.description: What was decided, counted from the decision when it is handed over, with an optional verdict.

summary.description: How the app sums up the plugin's reviews: which arrays of the payload and the decision to count, grouped by which field, with a label and a tone (`danger`, `warning`, `info`, `success` or `neutral`) for each value. A plugin without one shows no summary. A summary that does not read costs the plugin its summaries.

command.description: Run through the shell in a copy of the folder.

build.description: The command that produces the bundle, such as `{"command": "npm ci && npm run build"}`. An install from a folder or a repository runs it; a release never does.

accept.description: The kinds it takes: extensions like `.glb` and media types like `model/gltf-binary` or `image/*`. A file matches by its name's extension or its media type.

max_size.description: The most one file may be, in bytes; at most the app's 100 MB, which is also the default.

max_count.description: The most files one review may carry; at most the app's 32, the default.

attachments.description: The files the plugin takes beside a payload, sent with `pinrail submit --attach`. The payload names each one `{"$attachment": "<name>"}`, and the view reads it with `plugin.attachment(name)`. Without this key a plugin takes none. A block that breaks these rules keeps the plugin from installing.

dev.description: Marks a plugin under development in the app's listings.
